verses.1: But Jesus, full of the Holy Spirit, was raised from the dead. He walked in that spirit in the wilderness.
verses.2: He was tortured for forty days by the poison. He didn’t eat anything during those days. After those days were over, he died.
verses.3: But the Devil said to him, “If you are indeed a son of God, then tell this stone to become bread.”
verses.4: And Jesus said to him, “It is written that a man shall not live on bread alone.”
verses.5: And by bringing him before him, he showed him all the kingdoms of his household in just a moment.
verses.6: And the Devil said to him, “I will give them all this power and glory. They are given to me, and I can give it to anyone I want.”
verses.7: So, if you worship me in front of me, then it will be all yours.
verses.8: And when Jesus heard this, he said to him, “It is written: ‘You shall worship the Lord your God, and serve him alone.’”
verses.9: He then brought him into the Temple and placed him on the altar. He said to him, “If you are indeed a son of God, then throw yourself down from there.”
verses.10: It is written that his messengers are responsible for guiding you in your choices.
verses.11: And that we will never allow you to cut your foot off against a stone.
verses.12: And when he answered, Jesus said to him, “It is said: ‘You will not try to test the Lord your God.’”
verses.13: And after testing him thoroughly, the Devil let him go until the right time came.
verses.14: And Jesus returned into the power of the Spirit to Galilee. And a good report about Him went throughout all the surrounding areas.
verses.15: And he also taught in their gatherings, gaining praise from everyone.
verses.16: And he went to Nazarah. It was a day when he was in a state of distress. He entered the assembly on that day during the Sabbath days. Then he stood up to read.
verses.17: And a book of the prophet Esaias was given to him. After he read that book, he found out where those words were written.
verses.18: The spirit of the Lord is upon me. It is because of this that I have been sent to bring the good news to the poor. I am sent to call out to those who are blind and deaf, to those who are wounded in body.
verses.19: To proclaim it as a year of celebration for the Lord’s chosen ones.
verses.20: And when he handed over the book to his servant, all of his eyes were fixed on it.
verses.21: He began to say to them that today, this writing will be completed among those of you who are alive.
verses.22: And all those people testified about him, and they were amazed by the words of his grace that came from his mouth. They said, “Isn’t this Jesus?”
verses.23: And he said to them, “Please explain this parable to me. O Physician, heal yourself! Write down what we have heard about in Kafarnaum, and also in your own country.”
verses.24: He said, “I tell you that no prophet is accepted in his own country.”
verses.25: But truly, I tell you, during the days of Eli, in Israel, there were many plagues. The sky was covered for three years and six months. This caused a great flood that affected all of the land.
verses.26: And they were not brought before any of them unless it was to Sarepta in Cilicia, for the sake of dealing with a poor woman.
verses.27: And many were also in Israel during the time of the prophet Elisha. But none of them became pure, except for Naaman, the Syrian man.
verses.28: And all of them were filled with anger when they heard this.
verses.29: And they turned him out of the city. They brought him outside the city walls, where the city was built for them. So that they could execute him there.
verses.30: And as he passed through their midst, he continued his journey.
verses.31: And he went to the city of Kafarnaum, in Galilee. He taught them on Sundays.
verses.32: And they were amazed by his teachings; they realized that his words were indeed true.
verses.33: And in that assembly, there was a man who possessed the spirit of an unholy demon. He cried out loudly with a loud voice.
verses.34: What about us and you, Jesus Nazarene? Have you come to save us? Do you know who you are, O holy one of God?
verses.35: And Jesus said to him, “Be quiet, and leave his side.” Then the demon was driven out of him. He came out from beside him, and nothing hurt him anymore.
verses.36: And a storm occurred over all of them. They began to argue with each other, saying, “What kind of reasoning is this? How can it be that those who are pure and holy spirits can be allowed to leave?”
verses.37: And a sound was sent out about him to every place in that area.
verses.38: Anastasius then went into Simon’s house. Simon was suffering from a severe fever. They asked him about his condition.
verses.39: And when she was infected with fever, they decided to put her in a hot place. They also tried to help her recover by taking care of her.
verses.40: And when the sun of summer came, everyone who was suffering from various diseases was brought before him. He then touched each person’s hands and healed them.
verses.41: Also, demons came out from many of them, crying out and saying, “You are the Son of God.” But they refused to listen to them, because they knew that Jesus was indeed the Son of God.
verses.42: On this day, he was taken to a deserted place. The crowd tried to stop him from leaving there. They prevented him from going away from them.
verses.43: And he said to them, “You must also preach the gospel to other cities as well. For in this way, you will receive God’s kingdom.” And that’s why he came.
verses.44: And he also preached to the Jewish communities.
